::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
# Book_21 — OrgPath and Federal AI Governance
:::


::: {.callout-note}
Federal agencies have inventoried more than 1,800 deployed and piloted AI systems under OMB M-25-21 — and almost none of those systems are governed at the identity layer. Service accounts with no owner, credentials that predate the system's ATO, AI agents acting inside Entra tenants with no OrgPath, no lifecycle process, and no ownership record: this is the hidden identity surface the federal AI expansion has created. This book shows how OrgPath's organizational-placement model governs the AI surface the same way it governs every other surface — by making the owning bureau, the authorization boundary, and the credential lifecycle deterministic rather than tribal.
:::

## Companion canon

For the normative specifications this narrative paraphrases:

- [ADR-112 — Federal AI Use Case Governance](/docs/adr/adr-112-federal-ai-usecase-governance.html) — M-25-21 IAM obligations, OMB inventory integration, and ATO drift signal; the binding canon source for this book.
- [ADR-092 — Active Governance](/docs/adr/adr-092-active-governance.html) — the control-plane/data-plane boundary and L0–L4 actuation ladder; agentic AI systems are governed data planes.
- [ADR-059 — SailPoint Adapter Family](/docs/adr/adr-059-sailpoint-adapter-family.html) — the `sailpoint-machine-identity` conformance slot that observes the AI identity surface.
- [ADR-054 — Single-ATO Reciprocity](/docs/adr/adr-054-single-ato-reciprocity.html) — ATO enumeration and reciprocity; the surface the OMB inventory's `have_ato` field reconciles against.
- [ADR-040 — Drift Engine](/docs/adr/adr-040-drift-engine.html) — the six-phase orchestrator; `DRIFT-COMPLIANCE::ato-gap` and shadow-AI findings run through it.
- [Architecture Decision Records](/docs/adr/index.html) — the binding record; this book is governed primarily by ADR-112, ADR-092, ADR-059, and ADR-040.
